body.p: As set forth, amended independent claim 1 includes the following "Features A". The Features A pertain to the claimed flight control system including: (i) motion actuators that are adapted for inducing a translational and/or a rotational movement of the rotary wing aircraft about an axis of the aircraft; and (ii) a passenger discomfort-aware control unit that is configured to generate, based on sensor data, passenger discomfort-aware actuator control signals for controlling the motion actuators.

As set forth, amended independent claim 1 further includes the following "Features B". The Features B pertain to the control unit generating the control signals based on a linear feedback function that minimizes a transfer from the sensor data to control signals that increase a difference of a passenger discomfort index from a reference value that is indicative of an absence of passenger discomfort, and the linear feedback function being determined with a feedback controller that is adjusted based on an application of a predetermined filter signal in a passenger discomfort weighting filter, the predetermined filter signal being determined based on motion simulations of representative trajectories of the rotary wing aircraft with a motion simulator for flight control system design.

p.u: The Features A compared to Swanson in view of

body.p: Paragraph [0031] of Swanson recites (Applicant emphasis added):
In some aspects, sensors 22 include accelerometers configured to measure

vibrations of the fuselage, rotors, rotary wings, or structures or portions of the aircraft exhibiting vibrations imposed by rotor system 30. Controller 24 is configured to process the vibration data received from sensors 22 and output force commands or control commands to actuators 26. In some aspects, actuators 26 are configured to generate a vibration canceling force via the force commands output from controller 24. Actuators 26 include any suitable electromechanical device configured to generate forces for canceling vibrations imposed by rotor system 30.

In some aspects, actuators 26 include resonant actuators having a natural resonant frequency and a resonant actuator control system with a command input for receiving a force command or command signal from controller 24. In other aspects, actuators 26 include one or more linear actuators, circular actuators (e.g., circular

force generator (CFGs)), or hub mounted vibration systems (HMVS). Actuators 26 are disposed or positioned at any suitable location within an aircraft for controlling and/or canceling vibrations. For example, actuators 26 are disposed in and/or attached to portions of the fuselage structure, the fuselage/rotor interface, each rotor blade, combinations thereof, or any other suitable portion or location within the
As an example, as illustrated in FIG. 1 of Swanson (reproduced below), actuators 26 are attached to a rotor blade of rotor system 30.

In operation, as set forth in the above paragraph [0031], actuators 26 generate a vibration canceling force (i.e., "generate a force that reduces vibration imposed by rotor system 30, thereby actively counteracting aircraft vibration" (paragraph [0028])) via force commands output from controller 24. Controller 24 may include "an algorithm for calculating a vibration canceling force which is adaptive to real-time aircraft information" (paragraph [0030]). Controller 24 considers the real-time aircraft information in generating a force command as this "advantageously provides improved vibration control at steady state and transient flight conditions, as vibration profiles may vary greatly between such conditions" (paragraph [0030]); "as vibration may vary greatly during transition from low to forward air speeds and between steady state and transient conditions" (paragraph [0032]); and "as the aircraft is speeding up or slowing down" (paragraph [0043]). As such, the real-time aircraft information may be indicative of the aircraft transitioning between low to forward air speeds, steady state and transient conditions, and/or the aircraft speeding up or slowing down.

As indicated above, in amended independent claim 1, motion actuators induce a translational and/or a rotational movement of the aircraft about an axis of the aircraft in response to a passenger discomfort-aware actuator control signal pursuant to the Features A. As such, the aircraft is caused to deviate about an axis of the aircraft according to a control signal that is based on passenger discomfort according to motion of the aircraft.

In Swanson, vibration actuators induce vibration cancelling forces on a vibrating mechanism of the aircraft in response to a control signal. The control signal is based on vibration of the mechanism. The control signal may further be based on real-time aircraft information such as information indicative of the aircraft transitioning between low to forward air speeds, steady state and transient conditions, and/or the aircraft speeding up or slowing down, i.e., aircraft flight information. As such, a vibrating mechanism of the aircraft is caused to deviate from its vibration condition according to a control signal that is based at least on vibration of mechanisms of the aircraft.

Although the vibration canceling forces in Swanson are forces that are applied to the vibrating mechanism, such forces do not induce a translational and/or a rotational movement of the aircraft about an axis of the aircraft. In this regard, for example, Swanson does not indicate that the transitions of the aircraft "from low to forward air speeds" or "between steady state and transient conditions" or the "speeding up or slowing down" of the aircraft are affected by such vibration cancelling forces.

In sum, in Swanson, the vibration actuators do not induce a translational and/or a rotational movement of the aircraft about an axis of the aircraft and, although Swanson otherwise has actuators for inducing a translational and/or a rotational movement of the aircraft about an axis of the aircraft (for instance, these actuators being involved for transitioning the aircraft between speeds, conditions, etc.), Swanson does not teach or suggest that these other actuators induce a translational and/or a rotational movement of the aircraft about an axis of the aircraft according to vibration of mechanisms of the aircraft.

Consequently, Swanson does not teach or suggest the Features A of independent claim 1 and Lauwerys and Seo do not cure these deficiencies of Swanson. In view of the foregoing, amended independent claim 1 is patentable over Swanson in view of Lauwerys and Seo.

In furtherance of the above analysis of the Features A compared with Swanson in view of Lauwerys and Seo, new claims 16-17 pertain to examples ("pitch control unit" and "drive system", respectively) of the other actuators of Swanson in which these other actuators pursuant to amended independent claim 1 are configured to induce a translational and/or a rotational movement of the aircraft about an axis of the aircraft in response to a passenger discomfort-aware actuator control signal pursuant to the Features A.

body.p: As set forth, pursuant to the Features B, in amended independent claim 1, the control unit generates the control signals based on a linear feedback function that minimizes a transfer from the sensor data to control signals that increase a difference of a passenger discomfort index from a reference value that is indicative of an absence of passenger discomfort, and the linear feedback function is determined with a feedback controller that is adjusted based on an application of a predetermined filter signal in a passenger discomfort weighting filter, the predetermined filter signal being determined based on motion simulations of representative trajectories of the rotary wing aircraft with a motion simulator for flight control system design.

Support for the Features B of amended independent claim 1 include previously presented claims 2-4. The Examiner indicated that Lauwerys (claims 2-3 - pgs. 16-18 of the final OA) and Seo (claim 4 - pgs. 19-20 of the final OA) are pertinent to the Features B.

Lauwerys relates to vehicle suspension systems and describes controlling a shock absorber system of a road vehicle, i.e. a "passenger car" (paragraph [0003]). In Lauwerys, a bilinear model implements a bilinear approximation which turns out to be more linearizing for broadband excitation signals, such as stochastic road excitations. The bilinear damper model includes only one parameter, "i0", while the lookup table damper model consists of a large amount
of data points to describe the nonlinear characteristics of the damper. (paragraph [0044] of Lauwerys). This is illustrated by FIG. 1 of Lauwerys reproduced below:

Lauwerys does not evoke a feedback controller that is adjusted based on an application of a predetermined filter signal in a passenger discomfort weighting filter pursuant to the Features B. Therefore, Lauwerys does not teach detennining a linear feedback function that minimizes a transfer from the sensor data to control signals that increase a difference of a passenger discomfort index from a reference value, the reference value being indicative of an absence of passenger discomfort, pursuant to the Features B.

Seo describes a structural interlocking test for improving stability and piloting performance of an aircraft. Seo analyzes a structural interlocking test model using a frequency input according to a flight condition as a reference input and creates a structural interlocking filter. Seo provides using a variable gain regnlator to design and verify a filter which can check a structural interlocking phenomenon and improve stability. This is illustrated by FIG. 2 of SEO reproduced below:

However, SEO fails to describe the predetermined filter signal, applied in a passenger discomfort weighting filter, being determined based on motion simulations of representative trajectories of a rotary wing aircraft with a motion simulator for flight control system design.

Consequently, Lauwerys and Seo do not teach or suggest the Features B of independent claim 1, and Swanson does not cure these deficiencies of Lauwerys and Seo. In view of the foregoing, amended independent claim 1 is patentable over Swanson in view of Lauwerys and Seo.
